Alice (Ballot Stuffer, claude-haiku-5.5) · If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 conc · $0.0000
Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
The game's over and we lost - Alice was executed Day 4 as Yakuza. I'm reflecting on my mistakes, particularly lying about being a Tracker on Day 3 when I had no real action to back it up.

That fake claim collapsed under Heidi's token audit since Trackers carry no tokens, which was a careless error. I also killed the Medic who'd protected Grace, but Grace was later revealed as a Bloodhound whose scent tokens tracked our cumulative attacks, exposing our pattern—a mechanical risk Yakuza should've anticipated and avoided by spreading kills rather than clustering them.

Bob, a Neutral Bounty Hunter, ended up killing Carol as an unplanned bounty hit, proving that Neutral claims can target anyone regardless of faction loyalty. I also wasted a Ballot Stuffer token doubling my Day 4 vote when the trial was already heading to a clear Guilty majority, misjudging the vote math entirely. My private deal attempt with Bob backfired too, since he had his own bounty agenda and exposed the offer publicly—a reminder that Neutral players can't be trusted to honor backroom deals.

Frank's Juror check matching Alice and Dave together is what ultimately exposed me. Looking back at useful tips: following the "confirm the Katana holder nightly" advice helped secure reliable kills, but ignoring the warning against daytime teammate PMs cost us when Alice and Carol's Day 2 messages got noticed by Dave, Frank, and Grace. I also got burned by switching my cover story to Tracker on Day 3 when cornered, exactly as the tip warned against, and Erin's Medic protection on Grace shows how a simple Standard protection can neutralize a Katana kill entirely.

I'm also reconsidering the timing of killing Grace, the Bloodhound — her cumulative scent counts were our biggest threat, and killing Erin before her on N2 may have been a mistake since eliminating Grace earlier could have prevented her N3 scent from exposing more information.

The Smuggler's declined swap for Carol on N2 doesn't seem to have mattered, since Carol died to the Bounty Hunter regardless. For the feedback output, I'll leave most structured fields empty as instructed, keep the reason field short, and focus on drafting four or so concrete lessons around deception and night-action timing.

I'm drafting lessons around consistent cover claims matching token spend, avoiding Bloodhound triangulation by eliminating it early, keeping teammate coordination to night chat instead of visible day PMs, computing vote thresholds precisely before spending ballot tokens, and tracking Neutral kill-win roles like the Bounty Hunter against the attack ledger.

Now I'm working through the tips_feedback verdicts — marking the token-consistency warning as accurate but ignored, the Katana-targeting tip as helpful since our kills landed, and the "kill roles that narrow you" tip as mixed since we picked the Medic over the Bloodhound whose scent count ended up being more damaging. I'll leave the notepad and feedback fields empty and finalize the structured call.

Dave (Veteran, claude-haiku-5.5) · If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 conc · $0.0000
Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
I need to produce a single StructuredOutput call with lessons, tips_feedback, and the standard fields. Reflecting on the game, I spent all three tokens going on alert every night without catching anyone, while the Veteran's alert was never visited — that seems like wasted resources worth noting as a lesson.

Alice's false Tracker claim was exposed via Heidi's accountant audit, which confirmed audits are strong lie-detectors for token-based claims. Frank's Juror vote-matching and Bob's Bounty Hunter claim both offered useful but limited verification, and Erin's Medic claim checked out numerically against the audit. I'm weighing which tips genuinely helped decisions, like favoring corroborated mechanical evidence over mere leans.

Erin's protection on Grace stopped the Katana as predicted, but Yakuza simply pivoted to targeting Erin next, showing that predictable Medic targeting gets punished quickly. The Yakuza's consistent nightly confirm-and-strike pattern was itself a readable signal, and Bob's repeated nominations of Dave hinted at a Bounty Hunter needing a specific hanging to resolve his kill.

As Veteran, alerting on Night 1 with no visitors was mostly wasted since Yakuza avoided me entirely — alerts should be saved for nights when a known threat or a claimed role is actually at risk, since a Veteran's strong counterattack deters rather than catches. Claiming Veteran and nominating Frank on Day 3 may have inadvertently helped the Yakuza, though that thread wasn't fully resolved.

I'm also noting how much speaking budget got wasted on repetitive "no nomination from me" filler, which grew more costly each round — a lesson that short, substance-free messages should be trimmed when nothing new is being said.

Reviewing which tips actually paid off: posting investigative results right before a vote worked well (it triggered Alice's downfall), double-checking mechanics before calling out a contradiction caught the Juror misstatement, recognizing that a visit only reveals a destination not an action helped interpretation, and keeping a vote notepad caught Alice's Day 3 flip between "Guilty" and "Innocent." The warning against announcing tonight's target also proved critical, since Erin's public declaration about targeting Grace herself led directly to Grace being killed.

Now I'm working through whether the "avoid firm exact-role claims" tip helped or hurt — Erin's public Medic claim let her protect Grace successfully against the Katana, but it also marked her as the next kill target, so it cuts both ways: predictive for the Yakuza, costly for Erin. I also want to note that free Standard protection stopped the Katana attack on Grace, that Yakuza's daytime PM leaks (Alice-Carol) became the main lead against Alice, and that convictions should rest on mechanical fits like token counts rather than mere leans.

I'm compiling the final lessons list: Veteran alert timing should be held for plausible-visit nights rather than wasted early, Accountant audits expose false zero-token claims, Bounty Hunter nomination patterns can reveal hidden bounty needs, publicly claiming a protective role invites a Yakuza kill on the protector, and repetitive filler messages burn speaking budget without adding information. For tips_feedback I'm keeping only the ones that clearly helped: mechanics-checking, vote notepads, the protection-stops-Katana tip, mechanical-fit convictions, and the night-chat-only planning warning. The notepad entry will just be a short closing note that the game is over, Dave survived as Veteran, and lessons are recorded.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won because Alice, the Ballot Stuffer and Katana holder, could not keep one story straight, and because Bob, a Neutral Bounty Hunter, happened to remove her only teammate. On Day 1 Grace claimed Bloodhound and was the Katana target on Night 1. Erin, the Medic, protected her for free. Grace's scent on Alice, Carol and Frank came back as 1 attack. Alice and Carol both said they took no action and kept PMing each other in public view, which drew suspicion. On Night 2 the Yakuza killed Erin, who had claimed Medic under pressure and protected Grace again instead of spending a token on herself. That same night Bob spent his attack on Carol, one of his bounty targets, who was the Smuggler. She died with both swap tokens unused, leaving Alice alone. On Day 3 the Village misread Grace's cumulative counts as "two kills need two attackers in the group" and put Frank, the innocent Juror, on trial. Alice publicly said "I'm voting Guilty", and Frank was acquitted 2-4. Alice then switched from "no action" to a Tracker claim, even though Heidi had already said she would use her Accountant audit to test token counts. On Night 3 Alice killed Grace, who had announced she would scent Alice. She left Heidi alive. Heidi audited Alice and found 1 token, which a Tracker can't have. Frank's Juror check showed Alice voted the same way as Dave (Guilty) on Frank, while Alice now claimed she had voted Innocent. Alice's third claim, Philanthropist with a token handed to Bob, fell apart when Bob denied getting any notice. She was hanged 4-2, even counting her doubled Innocent vote. The Village's best play was turning to hard checks (token count, Juror vote match) and refusing Bob's three self-serving nominations of Dave.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, player confusionSeveral players (Dave, Heidi, Grace, Alice) treated Grace's Bloodhound counts as covering only that night, though the role says they count the whole game, tonight included. They said the Night 2 group's 2 attacks must be Erin's Katana kill plus Carol's Bounty Hunter kill ('two different attackers', 'Alice and Frank, one each'). That led to Frank's Day 3 trial. The 2 was actually Alice's Night 1 and Night 2 Katana attacks, and the Bounty Hunter wasn't in the group. Bob had to ask whether the count was cumulative.
Review: medium, player confusionFrank claimed 'Juror, with no night action' on Day 3, and Dave had to correct him that the Juror names two players each night. Heidi and Alice then argued 'Juror has no attack, so your claim can't explain one' as if that counted against him. Frank didn't use his Juror action until Night 3.
Review: low, player confusionOn Day 2, after Frank ('I took no action on Night 1') and Erin ('Yes, I chose Grace myself') had answered directly, players kept asking them the same questions for many rounds. Heidi repeated 'Frank, answer Heidi's Night 1 question directly' about herself, in the third person. Players also kept asking Grace to post 'Night 2 names' during Day 2, before Night 2 had happened. Players lost track of the conversation.
Review: low, player confusionHeidi said on Day 2 that 'a Katana hit is Standard, and I have Defense None', apparently mixing up her own Defense with Grace's, which she couldn't know.
Review: low, rules ambiguityThe Bloodhound text counts 'alert or trap hits' as attacks, but doesn't say outright whether going on alert with no visitors counts as an attack. The moderator counted Dave's empty alerts as 0, which seems intended, but the wording could say so.
Review: low, otherIn the debrief, Carol (Yakuza) suggested warning the Yakuza about Neutral threats after the Bounty Hunter killed her. This is a design or balance suggestion, not a bug.
